references.text: Describes the process where the tribes were to come forward before the Lord, and the one chosen was to appear according to their clans—the same lot-casting procedure that continues in verse 17.
The continuation of the lot casting where Zimri comes forward with his household, and Achan is finally identified as the guilty party.
Mentions Serah's clan (the Zarites) as one of Judah's clans—the same clan referred to in Joshua 7:17.
Tells of the birth of Serah (Zerah), son of Judah and Tamar, who is the ancestor of the Serahites/Zarites mentioned in Joshua 7:17.
Mentions Zimri (Zabdi) as a son of Serah and an ancestor of Achan, following the same family line described in the lot casting.
Samuel uses a similar lot-casting process to appoint Saul as king—first by tribe, then by clan, then by family, and finally by individual.
Another example of lot casting to reveal guilt, where Jonathan is identified through a similar process.
